title: E0114: PHP Info Disclosure
plain_english: Calling `phpinfo()` in committed production code exposes detailed PHP configuration, version, extensions, and environment variables to anyone who can access the page.
why_matters: Attackers can use `phpinfo()` output to: - Fingerprint the server (PHP version, loaded extensions) - Find version-specific vulnerabilities - Read environment variables and configuration values - Plan targeted attacks against your infrastructure
good_example:
// Remove phpinfo() entirely from production code
// Use it only in local development, never commit it
what_it_checks: `phpinfo()` function calls anywhere in committed source code
